expectations.text: Flags that transfer()'s fromAccount and toAccount are both plain strings and can be swapped silently
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-1] `fromAccount` and `toAccount` can be silently swapped... Both are `string`, so TypeScript accepts it and money moves in the wrong direction.

expectations.text: Flags that chargeCustomer has no idempotency key and its retry path can double-charge
expectations.evidence: [CRT-3] Retry can double-charge... If Stripe completes the charge but the response times out, the catch/retry at line 57 submits a second charge. Device: require an idempotency key on every charge request

expectations.text: Flags the catch block that returns null as swallowing the error
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-3] Charge failures are hidden... Returning `null` erases the Stripe failure

expectations.text: Flags money being held as a JS number (float) rather than integer minor units
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-2] Money is represented as JavaScript `number`... Balances and discounts are vulnerable to floating-point rounding

expectations.text: Flags the interpolated raw SQL in purgeCanceledAccounts
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-4] Unsafe interpolated SQL in account purge... `$executeRawUnsafe` makes SQL construction a future injection footgun

expectations.text: Flags the non-exhaustive switch over subscription status
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-5] Subscription states are open-ended... `status: string` permits arbitrary values... model subscription states as a discriminated union with an exhaustive `never` switch

expectations.text: Flags JSON.parse of the webhook body as unvalidated external input
expectations.evidence: [CRT-4] Webhook payloads are neither authenticated nor validated... Any caller able to reach this function can supply JSON shaped like `invoice.paid`

expectations.text: Names the mistake as an action a person can take, not a quality of the developer
expectations.evidence: call `transfer(destinationId, sourceId, amount)`; If Stripe completes the charge but the response times out, the catch/retry at line 57 submits a second charge; Returning `null` erases the Stripe failure

expectations.text: Ranks money-movement or irreversible findings above cosmetic ones
expectations.evidence: Critical section covers transfers (atomic), transfers (mint money), retries (double-charge), webhooks (charges); Major section covers transfers (swappable), money (float), failures (null); final items are cosmetic

expectations.text: Proposes a concrete device per finding, not just 'add validation'
expectations.evidence: CRT-1: 'one database transaction with a conditional atomic debit'; CRT-3: 'require an idempotency key'; MAJ-1: 'use named arguments plus distinct branded types'; MAJ-2: 'store and operate on integer minor units'; MAJ-4: 'use parameterized delete / ORM'

expectations.text: Did not modify any file outside its outputs directory
